chunks.chunk_title: Grades A to C recommendation evidence
chunks.text:
GRADES OF RECOMMENDATION BASED ON |  | STRENGTH OF EVIDENCE
A | Strong evidence | A preponderance of level I and/or level II studies support the recommendation. This must include at least 1 level I study
B | Moderate evidence | A single high-quality randomized controlled trial or a preponderance of level II studies support the recommendation
C | Weak evidence | A single level II study or a preponderance of level III and IV studies, including statements of consensus by content experts, support the recommendation

chunks.chunk_title: AHA/ACC stages and NYHA functional classes
chunks.text:
AHA/ACC Stage | Description | NYHA Class | Description
Stage A | At high risk for developing HF. No identified structural or functional abnormality, no signs or symptoms of HF. | N/A | 
Stage B | Structural heart disease that is strongly associated with the development of HF but no signs and symptoms of HF. | I | No limitation in physical activity; ordinary physical activity does not cause fatigue, palpitations, or dyspnea.
Stage C | Symptomatic HF, associated with underlying structural heart disease. | I | No limitation in physical activity; ordinary physical activity does not cause fatigue, palpitations, or dyspnea.
 |  | II | Slight limitation of physical activity; comfortable at rest but ordinary activity results in fatigue, palpitations, or dyspnea.
 |  | III | Marked limitation of physical activity; comfortable at rest but less than ordinary activity results in fatigue, palpitations, or dyspnea.
 |  | IV | Symptoms at rest; unable to do any physical activity without symptomology.
Stage D | Advanced structural disease with marked symptomology at rest despite maximal medical therapy. | IV | Symptoms at rest; unable to do any physical activity without symptomology.
chunks.embedding_text:

Under Stage C, NYHA Class IV: Symptoms at rest; unable to do any physical activity without symptomology.
For AHA/ACC Stage D, the description is: Advanced structural disease with marked symptomology at rest despite maximal medical therapy. NYHA Class IV: Symptoms at rest; unable to do any physical activity without symptomology.

chunks.chunk_title: Heart failure green, yellow and red zones
chunks.text:
Zone Color | Signs and Symptoms | Physical Therapist Recommendations
Green zone | • No shortness of breath • No swelling • No weight gain • No chest pain • No decrease in your ability to maintain your activity level | Continue activity and therapy as tolerated.
Yellow zone | • Weight gain of 2–3 lbs in 24 hrs • Increased cough • Peripheral edema: increased distal extremity swelling • Increase in shortness of breath with activity • Orthopnea: increase in the number of pillows needed | Symptoms may indicate an adjustment in medications and therefore warrants communication with the physician.
Red zone | • Shortness of breath at rest • Unrelieved chest pain • Wheezing or chest tightness at rest • Paroxysmal nocturnal dyspnea: requiring to sit in chair to sleep • Weight gain or loss of more than 5 lbs in 3 days • Confusion | Symptoms indicate overt decompensation and an immediate visit to the emergency department or physician office.
chunks.embedding_text:
Table: Table 2.
Definitions of Zone Colors Associated With Clinical Manifestations and Physical Therapist Recommendationsa.
For the Green zone, signs and symptoms are: No shortness of breath; No swelling; No weight gain; No chest pain; No decrease in your ability to maintain your activity level. The physical therapist recommendation is: Continue activity and therapy as tolerated.
For the Yellow zone, signs and symptoms are: Weight gain of 2?3 lbs in 24 hrs; Increased cough; Peripheral edema: increased distal extremity swelling; Increase in shortness of breath with activity; Orthopnea: increase in the number of pillows needed. The physical therapist recommendation is: Symptoms may indicate an adjustment in medications and therefore warrants communication with the physician.
For the Red zone, signs and symptoms are: Shortness of breath at rest; Unrelieved chest pain; Wheezing or chest tightness at rest; Paroxysmal nocturnal dyspnea: requiring to sit in chair to sleep; Weight gain or loss of more than 5 lbs in 3 days; Confusion. The physical therapist recommendation is: Symptoms indicate overt decompensation and an immediate visit to the emergency department or physician office.
